messages:
Alex Carter: FYI — I just got a request from data-team for a 48x A100 reservation in us-west-2 for Q1 training. Lead time estimate from vendor is ~22 days, they want it in 7. :grimacing:
Priya Nair: Ouch. What priority? Can they accept spot or burst capacity as a stopgap?
Alex Carter: They explicitly want reserved capacity with SLA. Said they'll sign a 6‑month commitment if we can guarantee a hard start date within 10 days.
Jamie Chen: Current reserved pool only has ~12 free A100s in us-west-2. There's a maintenance window next week that decommissions ~200 old nodes (affects scheduling).
Ben Ortiz: Can we split the job across regions and stitch via secure transfer? Might be cheaper than expanding reserved commit fast.
Carla Mendez: Not possible due to data residency — dataset is internal/proprietary and the customer requires us-west-2 only unless legal signs an addendum.
InfraBot: Reservation request #84321 status updated: moved to escalation_queue by Alex Carter at 1915005555
Liam O'Connor: Quick billing flag — front-loading a 48-GPU reserved commitment will change our cloud committed use discounts and could lower per-token cost, but increases exposure to utilization risk.
Priya Nair: Could we propose a phased ramp: 24 GPUs initially, +24 after 10 days? That keeps them productive and reduces immediate strain.
Jamie Chen: Phased ramp is technically feasible if they accept split start dates. Need to update autoscaling and placement policies though.
Alex Carter: Who can sign a manual lead-time exception? Our standard SLA assumes 21d vendor lead time. I need an approver to bypass that policy if LOI arrives.
Carla Mendez: I'm comfortable approving an exception for a signed commitment, but finance must sign off on the cost/risk. I'll draft the approval template (T&Cs, cancellation penalties).
Ben Ortiz: Action from my side: run cost delta across commit lengths (6mo vs 1yr) and include cross-region transfer penalties if we consider partial fallback.
Priya Nair: Action list: Alex — get LOI/signed intent; Jamie — draft phased deployment plan + autoscaling diff; Ben — cost delta spreadsheet; Carla — exception approval template + legal pointers.
Alex Carter: Timeline: aim to get LOI by EOD tomorrow. If we have it, we'll escalate to vendor for priority placement. :thumbsup:
InfraBot: Capacity-check snapshot for us-west-2 at 1915005620:
```
resvctl capacity-check --region us-west-2 --instance-type a100
Available: 12
Pending decomm: 200 scheduled 2025-11-03
Estimated vendor lead-time: 22d
```
Jamie Chen: We can try to reclaim up to ~8-10 GPUs by preempting lower-priority batch jobs in the next 48h. Will coordinate with job-ops.
Liam O'Connor: Finance note: penalties on early cancellation escalate non-linearly. If we commit and later scale down, risk grows. Need probability estimate of churn.
Priya Nair: If LOI comes in, Alex ping me and I'll start the formal exception sign-off thread with finance (I have the finance contact).
Carla Mendez: Approved process: exception request -> finance estimate -> legal addendum -> infra scheduling. I'll draft the form and push to shared drive.
Ben Ortiz: I'll share a quick spreadsheet in-thread with unit costs and break-even points for 3/6/12 month commits.
Alex Carter: If we don't get LOI by midday tomorrow, we'll offer phased + burst agreement and move forward.
Priya Nair: :eyes:
Jamie Chen: Follow-up: I'll post an autoscaler config snippet and an ansible task to pin nodes for the phased allocation.
Alex Carter: Thanks folks. Keeping this thread as the single source of truth; will update when LOI or vendor response arrives.
